pages.text: From erectus, press $(k:hominin_evolution.build) for what you know how to build: a $(l)small hut$() first, and once you have built one, a $(l)thatch tent$(). Each turns in front of you, with what it takes - thatch blocks and building branches from the work station.$(br2)Pick one and $(o)Plan it$().

Its $(l)ghost$() follows where you look, its doorway facing you: pale where it fits, red where it does not - it wants solid, level ground under all of it and nothing in the way. $(k:hominin_evolution.item_interact) marks it out there; $(k:hominin_evolution.build) puts the plan away.$(br2)The ghost stays. Place the right block where it shows - or use one on a ghost block to set it straight in. The wrong block will not go.

When the last block is in, it stands, and the band asks: $(o)what do we do with this?$()$(br2)Raw thatch rots in the weather; stretch hide over it (the roof will do - it shelters the wall under it) and it lasts. You can have three builds marked out at once. Your map shows them all.

$(li)$(l)A store$(): sneak-use its floor with food, bones or anything else you carry to lay it down - tools too. The hungry eat from it, bones get cracked for marrow, spare food is put by. No beds in it.$(li)$(l)Yours$(): nobody sleeps in it but you and your mate, and you wake rested.$(li)$(l)For the others$(): you choose who.

Giving someone a roof means more than anything you could hand them: bond +5. Give it to someone $(l)hurt$(), or $(l)carrying a child$(), and the whole band sees it - cohesion rises a long way.$(br2)They sleep in it - a nest of any size will do under a roof - and a hurt one mends twice as fast lying up in it. If they die, it stands empty, and you decide again.

Now and then one of the band will want something built - somewhere dry for someone hurt or with child, a store, a roof for you - and mark its $(l)ghost$() out on your ground, in yellow. Press $(k:hominin_evolution.build): $(o)Confirm$(), $(o)Move$() it, or $(o)Cancel$(). Until a block goes in, you can still move or cancel any plan.
